questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities and native English speaking country

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Over all it was very easy to find the information I needed to know upon arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was fine - easy to get in touch with the university if you had any questions.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was actually really difficult to find housing in Madison for some reason. Normally it is super easier, but there were expectational many exchange students in the Fall 2022. Therefore I ended up living off campus, which was fine but I would prefer to stay downtown next time. Try to look at different Facebook pages for housing, and you should not pay more than $1000 per month for a room.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is impossible to bike when it gets cold, so make sure that you can take the bus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Start your search early. I thought it would be easy to find housing, but it takes some time.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Good. Note that you have to contact the professor every time you want to enroll in a course. The usually reply within a day or two. You are not able to see the syllabus, but just contact the professor and they will send it.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You login to the homepage and find the courses you want. It is possible to register for more courses than you want, and then later on you can drop some of the courses (you have about two weeks to decide)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You are able to see your schedule immediately, which is very good. Make sure you don't have any classes on Fridays.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Write to the professors before hand, and make sure you are allowed to enroll before the registration opens.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic programme is good. The workload throughout the semester is huge compared to KU, but the finals are a bit easier.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It depends on the courses you take, but over all I would say the level is higher at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Be ready to participate in the lectures/classes, and many of the professors will cold call.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
305 - Financial Markets, Institutions and Economic Activity 
420 - Investment Banking and Capital Markets 
423 - Strategic Management 
740 - Fixed Income Analysis

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Don't take 423, the course level is way to low. 420 is good, but be ready to do a minimum of 4-5 hours of homework every week. 740 is interesting and the level is very high. If you want to learn about the US financial system then take 305.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: SHIP insurance (around $700). It does not make any sense, but you have to buy it.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are so many opportunities and many different events/clubs to check out.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kind of events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Watch college sport (Basketball, soccer, football, volleyball etc)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit Chicago, Minneapolis, Milwaukee, Devil's Lake, The House On The Rock, Green Bay, Cranberry Farm.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not a problem at all.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to participate in different events / clubs.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Friendliness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Bring a warm jacket for the cold months, try to find a place downtown and don't have any classes on Fridays.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Join Scan Design Program and remember to apply for the the scholarship as well.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The overall experience. Madison is a really cool city, and it is fun to experience a college city in the US.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Most of the American students are very young (18-20), so sometimes it is a challenge to socialize when you are a bit older.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
